tasks.short: Select, store, order, issue and inventory classroom supplies

steps.what: Select suitable classroom equipment, materials and supplies for student needs
Count and inspect selected stock and capture quantities and locations
Record classroom inventory and reconcile equipment and supply records
Prepare and approve orders for required classroom items
Store and issue classroom equipment and supplies safely

tasks.design: Configure a classroom stock list in {PROCUREMENT} or its native inventory module, reusing identifiers instead of copying between {SPREADSHEET} and order forms. Keep suitability selection, physical count, storage, issue and final order approval human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inventory and order records may repeat the same item and quantity details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native stock lists and saved catalogue lines can reuse those details.
tasks.still_hard: Accessible equipment suitability and condition cannot be established from a stock total.
tasks.human_edge: Choose materials that fit actual students and recognise unsafe or unsuitable equipment.
tasks.altitude: Less inventory and order entry, with unchanged educational and physical responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Native inventory and order-line reuse and the proposed savings are E1 design assumptions; no school-supply case is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is teacher selection, inventory, ordering, storage and issue; supplier delivery and purchasing-team approval beyond delegated teacher authority are excluded and unchanged.

Teacher in s2 produces item identifier, count, unit, condition, location and check date, with all capture retained in 20 full hours. Teacher selects required quantity in retained s4 time; no par level or shortage flag is assumed to exist.

Existing catalogue administrator maintains item, supplier, pack unit and price fields in the unchanged catalogue. Missing identifiers or unsuitable mappings require manual inventory and order entry within retained s3 and s4 time.

Test native inventory and saved order lists first. Three focal upkeep hours cover item lists and mappings. s5 covers handling of available stock independently of whether an order is placed in the same cycle.
unknowns: Actual duplicate entry and native inventory support
Teacher's spending authority and equipment checks
research_questions: Can reuse halve inventory entry and cut order entry by 40% after reconciliation and approvals?

already_counted.description: Physical count and structured stock capture
Inventory reconciliation and manual entry fallback
Quantity selection, order checks and approval

incremental.description: Maintain classroom item lists and order mappings

approvals.approved_version: Final order snapshot with items, quantities, units, supplier, prices, delivery terms and destination; changes void approval before release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=84, gross=16 minus 3 upkeep gives net=13. High assumes recurring inventory and catalogue copying; low assumes only 3 hours removable. Selection, physical count and handling retain 65 full hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit schools to tutor sensory-impaired students and consult teachers

steps.what: Gather authorised student support records and lesson material for the school visit
Visit schools and tutor students with sensory impairments using appropriate accessible methods
Consult school teachers regarding students' special needs and practical support

tasks.design: Configure source-linked visit packs in {DOCS} and {LMS} from existing authorised material. Keep travel, accessible tutoring, adaptation during the lesson and consultation fully with the specialist teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant versions of existing support records and lesson material are gathered repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links can collect selected records without rewriting their clinical or educational meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Sensory access needs and classroom conditions require direct observation and specialist teaching.
tasks.human_edge: Notice how the student responds and help teachers make practical adjustments.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less pack collection, with unchanged specialist teaching and consultation authority.

reach.task: Adapt classroom practice for sensory access
reach.learn: How specialist recommendations work in everyday lessons

evidence.claim: Source-linked visit preparation and the proposed saving are E1 design assumptions; the digest does not establish sensory tutoring or travel automation.

assumptions: Boundary is specialist preparation, school travel, tutoring and consultation. Travel is included in the fully retained s2 share; school teachers' participation is outside the focal denominator and unchanged.

Existing support-plan author and lesson author produce records with student or lesson reference, version and date. Specialist selects purpose, sources and permissions in retained s1 time, including manual collection when links are missing; no structured impairment code is assumed.
Pack contains source records rather than inferred support judgements. New accessible-material creation is not credited as retrieval savings and would require separate estimation.
Native document links precede code. Two focal upkeep hours cover pack links and access checks.
unknowns: Existing records, cross-school permissions and actual preparation share
research_questions: Can source linking reduce collection by 40% while preserving all travel, tutoring and consultation time?

already_counted.description: Source selection, permission checks and manual collection

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=94, gross=6 minus 2 upkeep gives net=4. High assumes reusable authorised sources; low assumes only 2 preparation hours saved. Travel, tutoring and consultation retain 85 full hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some supply administration and visit preparation may shrink; accessible teaching and direct consultation remain central.
role.ambitious_version: Provide consistent practical sensory-access support with dependable classroom resources and well-prepared school visits.
